title: Three Nights, Again

time: 18:30 the evening 3.3 ends, then three nights in Ward 4 (sleep → 07:00 each morning, as at the hotel)
player_goal: Get through three nights in the ward until the doctor signs.
design_goal: An echo of the first week (0.2: three hotel nights, a countdown, the city opening up) played backwards: three ward nights, the same countdown, and the city closing down. Nothing attacks; the phone simply gets quieter each morning, the ward empties, the sounds outside thin out, and on the third morning Ravi's bed is empty. Dread by subtraction.

cast.role: Evening 1: 'Three nights. Then the doctor signs — Thursday.' Day 2: busier, shorter. Day 3, asked about Ravi: 'Moved. Another ward. Don't ask me which.'
Day 1: 'They took my phone. For tests, they said.' Day 2: asleep, a cough he didn't have before. Night 3: gone — the bed stripped, the IV line on the floor.

beats.what: 18:30, back from the corridor. Sister Lalitha: 'Three nights. Then the doctor signs.' The hotel's countdown plate comes back under the clock: 'Discharge · 3 nights'. Your bed now works (sleep → 07:00), as the hotel's did.

Morning 1. News: 'BBMP announces night curfew, 10 PM–6 AM, "as a precaution"' (the TV ticker says the same). Ravi: 'They took my phone. For tests, they said.' The city through the window is quieter (fewer horns).

Morning 2. Amma: 'Come home. Please. Your father is asking.' — two replies, both kind, neither a yes. The woman's bed across the aisle is empty. The tapping at the isolation door has stopped. Ravi asleep, a cough he didn't have. The UPI app: 'Server busy. Try again later.' (payments still go through).

Morning 3. Ravi's bed stripped; his IV line on the floor; the green lanyard gone from the locker. Sister Lalitha: 'Moved. Another ward. Don't ask me which.' The signal drops to nothing. The countdown reads 'Discharge · today'. (3.5 Discharge starts here.)
